Summary: Complaints centre on land and revenue grievances in Behat tehsil, illegal Yamuna mining and unsafe travel on the Delhi-Yamunotri highway, while canal irrigation, mango orchards and handicrafts are the main points of appreciation, though local evidence is thin and several items are inference.
Field-check notes: Identity confirmed from the Wikipedia UP constituency list (No. 1 Behat, district Saharanpur, reserved status None, 372,305 electors) and the Behat constituency page (formed 2008; MLA Umar Ali Khan, SP, elected 2022). Wikipedia's Behat town article gives population as 8,574 in the infobox and 20,474 in the census text, so it is internally inconsistent; not used. Round 2 budget: about 16 WebFetch and 14 WebSearch calls in total across both rounds. Coverage is still thin. Behat AC boundary: neither the Wikipedia constituency page nor any search result listed the villages in the AC. Mirzapur and Shakumbhari could not be confirmed as inside Behat AC (Shakumbhari is cited only as a Ghad-area flood story, not used). Sarsawa is said in search snippets to be partly merged into Behat in 2008, but this was not confirmed on a fetched page. Two parliamentary records (eparlib.sansad.in 9401.pdf and 7412.pdf) appeared in search and describe Yamuna erosion threatening dozens of Behat villages (Ninhari, Jodhewas, Kansepur and others) and hill rivers (Solani, Hindon, Chachrao, Maskara, Nagadev, Ramaula). Both returned HTTP 503 on fetch, so they are NOT cited. They are a lead for field checks and a later round. An Amar Ujala 18 Sep 2025 report on flooded rivers near the Shakumbhari Devi shrine (Ghad area) was opened but does not name Behat, so it is not cited. Not found in any source: 2024-2026 Behat reports on cane dues, power cuts, roads, stray cattle, monkeys or water; the Patrika 1 Aug 2026 item on an SP MLC procession clash is political and was not used. Negative 4 (speeding, based on a 2021 crash), negative 5 (mango prices), and positives 4 and 5 are inference and need field checks. Only one Behat-specific 2025 report was found (Amar Ujala, 21 Feb 2025). The Behat mining item is police-station-level; its village boundary is unconfirmed.

Amar Ujala 2021 and the Public App feed were verified against their text. Removed: the dowry reference (not on the feed); the Wikipedia source for the 'markets' positive (no market source found, the item was dropped); the roads and power negative (no road or power source was found in any search, so the item was removed rather than kept as a guess). Several cited sources were not usable: the Ministry of Civil Aviation Sarsawa airport page and the Hindustan Times 2023 Gurjar-rally page returned HTTP 403, the UniIndia Ambheta/Didoli page returned HTTP 404, and a Saharanpur police PRP PDF (April 2026, Nakur police sand tractors on the Yamuna) could not be read as text, so none of them is cited. Patrika search-result dates of 2026 for the flood articles were page-banner dates; the articles are from 2018. Searches found no 2024-26 Nakur or Sarsawa report on sugarcane dues, roads, water, power, Krishni-river mining, or Nakur CHC, and 14 WebSearch calls were run this round and the search results were mostly from other districts. Field check recommended: Amar Ujala and Dainik Jagran Saharanpur pages for नकुड़, सरसावा, सुल्तानपुर and चिलकाना on water, power, roads, cane dues (2025-26), Yamuna flood status and embankment repair at Hathnikund, Krishni-river sand mining, and the Nakur CHC; verify the Public App headlines against the original Hindi outlets. P5 weak positive: only says municipal bodies exist; whether civic work is effective is not verified.

P3 weak positive: the article only announces the inauguration; completion is not confirmed. P4 weak positive: conditional statement; no 2024-26 report of on-time crushing was found. P5 weak positive: 2018 plan only; no 2024-26 progress report found.

Summary: Complaints centre on unpaid sugarcane dues owed by the Bajaj mill in the Nagal area, with farmers also raising crop-protection and power demands; most positives and several negatives remain unverified inference.

P2 weak positive: general statement, no facilities named and no year given. Nanauta and Gangoh are not named on that page, so they are not treated as part of this AC. Check against the ECI delimitation list before publishing. Verified in round 2: Amar Ujala 7 Jan 2023 memorandum, Amar Ujala 6 Feb 2023 Bajaj GM arrest, Royal Bulletin 5 Oct 2026 dues report, Wikipedia AC and town pages. The CropGPT aggregator (16 Jul 2026, memorandum and Nagal/urea/road claims) was fetched; it states the facts but names no original outlet, and the memorandum itself could not be found in any Hindi outlet, so every CropGPT-based claim was removed or turned into inference. Only one negative names an AC place (Nagal, via the Bajaj mill). Gangnauli village is described as in the Nagal area (Amar Ujala 2023) and in Deoband tehsil (plant directory); confirm it lies inside this AC. Negatives 2 and 3 (roads and urea) and positives 4 and 5 remain inference. Not reached: Dainik Jagran, Hindustan and Patrika Saharanpur editions were not indexed by the search tool for this AC; the Amar Ujala searches returned no Nagal or Rampur Maniharan local news. The ETV Bharat and Himachal Rampur results are a different Rampur and were excluded. Field check: Nagal and Rampur road condition after monsoon, urea availability at the Nagal cooperative society, Gangnauli mill dues for 2025-26, nilgai damage in 2025-26, and local medical facilities named in the town.

Summary: Complaints centre on tyre-factory smoke and the deadly Kallarheri clash that followed, with power cuts and river encroachment also raised; cane dues remain unverified for Gangoh.
Field-check notes: Voice pass (round 3, text only): P1 reworded as appreciation of planned roads; P2, P3 and P5 reworded; N1 to N5 reworded to voter voice, with English aligned to Hindi. P2 weak positive: pending proposal, and the benefit depends on state approval. P3 weak positive: administrative action over a records lapse (death-certificate portal), not a fix for residents. The Gangoh AC extent (Ambehta, Gangoh, Titron, Nanauta and NPs) comes from the Wikipedia AC page; the village-level membership of Kallarheri and Sindhali villages (Alampur, Sukhedi) is inferred from 'Gangoh area/block' wording and not separately confirmed against the electoral roll. Panchayat-secretary item is administrative, not a resident complaint; it is kept only as an official action. Electoral and MLA details excluded per brief.

Summary: Complaints centre on town roads and drains never built, power cuts that also stop water, and sugarcane dues; appreciation is limited to partial mill payments, police arrests and action against unapproved colonies.

Positive 3 comes from a Shamli Police press release (1 Sep 2025), so it states police action only; no resident feeling of safety is claimed because the basis does not state one. Summary: Complaints centre on smart-meter power cuts, waterlogged Shamli city markets, Jal Jeevan Mission-damaged roads and hospital services, while appreciation is limited to a sugar mill payment, a bill relief scheme and a city underpass under construction.
Field-check notes: Voice pass (round 3, text only): all positives 1 to 5 and negatives 1 to 5 reworded to voter voice, with English aligned to Hindi and full stops removed. POSSIBLY OUTDATED: P2, the bill relief scheme, ran 1 Dec 2025 to 28 Feb 2026 and has ended (basis), so keep it only as a historical item and check before publishing. N1 is a consumers' account; the SE said disconnection was for non-recharged meters. P5 is a proposal only, with no site found yet. Search budget: about 25 WebSearch calls total (6 in round 1, 19 in round 2), plus about 20 page fetches. Verified every cited URL by fetch; the Oon, Thana Bhawan and Mansura sources were fetched and found to support their facts, but those places are outside AC 10 so they were removed. Kandhla AC membership rests on the undated Wikipedia AC page (lists 'Kandhala'); check against the ECI delimitation order before field use. Shamli district hospital and Shamli city markets are assumed to lie in Shamli town (Shamli tehsil, wholly in AC 10 per Wikipedia), not verified against a map. Still unverified: AC location of Kabaudh bridge and Shamli chini mill. Positives are mostly district-level; the only AC-town positive is the Bhainswal underpass, whose June 2026 opening is not confirmed. The bill relief scheme ended 28 Feb 2026 and is historical. No 2026 sugarcane-dues negative with an AC-specific source was found (remaining cane-dues reports concern Thana Bhawan or Oon). Not found: 2026 Shamli city road or drain complaints, stray cattle reports for Shamli, completed Shamli city road/bridge inaugurations, Kendriya Vidyalaya land outcome. Excluded: 2021 Shamli city waterlogging article (4 Aug 2021), 2022 Oon mill ADM article, 2025 Shamli smart-meter statements not re-checked. Hindi AC name and place spellings (कांधला, आल्दी, काबड़ौत) are as printed in the sources, not checked against an official Hindi source.

Summary: Delayed cane payments from the Budhana (Bhaisana) sugar mill and dangerous traffic on the Budhana-Muzaffarnagar road dominate complaints, with narrow lanes near Bhainsana also raised, while an approved Luhsana cane purchase centre and a sanctioned dispensary for seven Budhana villages are the main positives.
Field-check notes: Identity confirmed from Wikipedia 'Budhana Assembly constituency': Constituency No. 11, Muzaffarnagar, reservation None. Its extent is 'Budhana Tehsil' except five polling-centre areas (Nala, Taharpur Bhabisa, Kaniyan, Salfa, Sunna). Region Paschim UP is my assignment (Wikipedia has no region column). BHAINSANA AND LUHSANA: Luhsana is confirmed as a Budhana village by Royal Bulletin (4 Oct 2026), which covers seven Budhana villages including Luhsana. Bhainsana/Bhaisana is described as being in the Budhana area by Navbharat Live and as 'the Bhainsana region near the Budhana sugar mill' by ChiniMandi, but no source lists it in the AC or Budhana tehsil village list; the Wikipedia page does not name it. Treat Bhainsana's AC membership as likely but not fully confirmed; field check or the Factbook village list (indiastatpublications Budhana Factbook, 2011 panchayat list) would settle it. Verification: all 7 unique URLs were opened and checked. The ChiniMandi 13,000-farmers item was dropped because the Ground News excerpt cut off before the figure, and it was not a benefit voters would appreciate. Two of the negatives (Tabalshah Road, Muzaffarnagar city; power cuts) are city/district-level and not Budhana-specific, so only 3 of 5 negatives count as AC-specific, and only if Bhainsana is in the AC. Items with no Budhana-specific source: water supply, drains, power in Budhana, and stray cattle. Searches (about 15 rounds, Hindi and English) found no Budhana-specific 2025-26 reports on these; a Muzaffarnagar municipal drainage tender story (Amar Ujala, 17 Sep 2026) concerns the city, not Budhana, and was not used. Original Hindi sources not found for ChiniMandi items (ChiniMandi is English) or for the 339.65 crore figure; the Ground News pages are aggregators. The positive mill payment schedule (Apr 2025) is an agreed schedule, not proof of payment. The Bajaj Hindusthan Budhana unit name comes from a search snippet only, not fetched. Field check recommended for all Budhana-level water, drains, power and cattle items. P3 weak positive: the payment dates are from April 2025 and compliance is not shown. P4 weak positive: the source shows the bus service runs, but not its frequency or reliability. P5 weak positive: district-level figure dated April 2025, not Budhana-specific.

Summary: Complaints centre on delayed sugarcane dues, erratic power, a municipal sanitation and tax dispute, waterlogging from poorly cleaned drains and a dilapidated Bhainsi nala bridge, while the strongest positives are the Triveni sugar mill and NH-58 trade links.
Field-check notes: Identity confirmed from the Wikipedia AC page (Constituency No. 15, Khatauli, Muzaffarnagar, reserved status None). Region set to Paschim UP by assignment because the Wikipedia infobox only says 'North India'. The Wikipedia AC page lists Madan Bhaiya (RLD) as incumbent, elected 2022; it also has a 2027 results section with no vote figures. Political items were excluded per the brief. Round 2 result: three Khatauli-specific negatives (sanitation dispute May 2026, Bhainsi nala bridge 2022, rajwaha waterlogging Nov 2025). No Khatauli-specific 2024-2026 positive was found. Searches that found nothing for Khatauli: Triveni Khatauli mill cane dues 2026, NH-58 jams at Khatauli, Khatauli power cut protests, Bhainsi nala bridge completion. The Wire item was dropped because only its headline was available. The Dainik Bhaskar original could not be fetched, so the power item relies on the Ground News summary. P4 weak positive: a government office building, not a direct service. P5 weak positive: an official claim that residents dispute (see N2).

Summary: Voters in Chamraua mostly complain of no development in five years, unemployment and inflation, overflowing drains and unchecked ploughing of government land, while appreciating timely fertiliser and subsidy transfers, a near-complete polytechnic building and some scheme benefits.

P2 weak positive: a building only, classes not yet started. P3 weak positive: general, no scheme named. P4 weak positive: building only; as of June 2025 lab technician recruitment was awaited. P5 weak positive: partial recovery only (Nov 2024), one accused still absconding. N4 reason per district school inspector: student numbers kept falling; institutional item, no student or parent voice in the source.

P3 weak positive: approval only, no work started. P4 weak positive: approval and tendering only. P5 weak positive: one first-aid incident, no resident praise.
